problems.description: 82 naming violations across index.ts, dev-server.ts, markdown.ts (classes/interfaces not PascalCase, functions not camelCase, constants not UPPER_CASE) — convention score 0.53 in the very first scaffolding commit
Cognitive complexity +45 across only 3 new functions suggests over-dense logic seeded early in the greenfield codebase
SonarQube reports +2 new bugs on a greenfield baseline; a clean scaffold should introduce zero
+3 code smells in the initial scaffold will compound across subsequent sessions

strengths: Sensible greenfield toolchain: ts-jest preset, jest, typescript — consistent with a CLI/SSG project shape
package-lock.json committed (lockfileVersion 3) — reproducible, pinned dependency resolution
Standard SSG stack (gray-matter + marked) fits the static-site-generation task domain
Zero duplication (0.0%) in the new code
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally reasonable greenfield scaffolding for an SSG (good stack + lockfile, zero duplication), but convention adherence is weak at 0.53 — 82 naming violations and 2 bugs seeded in session 1 set a debt baseline for the rest of the story.

problems.description: CLI arg-parsing is duplicated: the serve branch reimplements the same flag loop as the build branch instead of sharing one parser, only adding --port handling.
Convention score 0.53 with 82 violations across new/touched files (dev-server.ts, index.ts, markdown.ts): functions not camelCase, classes/interfaces not PascalCase, constants not UPPER_CASE.
Cognitive complexity +62 from the dense serve/dev-server wiring (watcher startup, WebSocket reload, file serving) could be decomposed into smaller helpers.
Runtime dependency surface grows by two packages (chokidar, ws) for the dev server; justified for the shipped feature, but it couples serve logic into the main bundle.

strengths: Type-safe CLI extension: ParseResult union widened with ServeOptions and ServeOptions extends BuildOptions, so option shapes stay shared and checked.
Thorough --port validation (numeric, 1-65535, rejects missing/flag-like values) and graceful SIGINT/SIGTERM shutdown via server.close().
Clean dependency hygiene: chokidar/ws as runtime deps, @types/ws as devDependency, lockfile updated consistently.
Serve/live-reload is idiomatically isolated into its own module, keeping cli.ts focused on argument handling.
commit_reviews.summary: Architecturally sound integration of a serve + live-reload subcommand with type-safe CLI extension and correct dependency hygiene, but the 0.53 convention score (82 naming violations) and duplicated arg-parsing add measurable maintainability debt.

problems.description: 82 convention violations per static analysis, yielding a convention score of 0.53 — flagged across index.ts, dev-server.ts, and markdown.ts (naming rules: classes/interfaces PascalCase, functions camelCase, constants UPPER_CASE).
Cognitive complexity +30 with 1 new smell concentrated in the 248-line dev-server.ts (live-reload injection + WebSocket lifecycle); a 'refactor' commit should ideally reduce, not grow, complexity.
loadConfig() uses require() on an arbitrary resolved path and silently swallows all errors, masking a misconfigured or non-loadable ssg.config with a fallback to defaults.

Three re-export shim files (plugins/dev-server.ts, markdown.ts, templates.ts) add an indirection layer; they preserve the public API, but every export added in src/plugins/ must now be mirrored in the shim.
No test files appear in the +12-file diff for the new PluginPipeline/SSGEngine lifecycle, which is the commit's core new surface.

strengths: Clean plugin architecture: a single PluginPipeline with well-named lifecycle hooks (onStart/beforeBuild/onFile/afterBuild/onEnd) mirrors established SSG patterns
SSGEngine.fromOptions() deduplicates plugins by name, giving deterministic composition of CLI/config/default plugins
Re-export shims preserve the existing public plugin API, so the refactor is backward compatible
Duplication decreased (-0.4%) and zero new bugs introduced despite +850/-403 lines of reorganization
Efficient parallel write of build outputs via Promise.all
commit_reviews.summary: Strong, backward-compatible architectural refactor extracting a proper engine + plugin pipeline with zero new bugs and reduced duplication, though the measured 0.53 convention score and +30 complexity temper the score — and I flag a discrepancy: the sample violations (PascalCase classes, camelCase functions) contradict the visible code, which follows those rules correctly, suggesting the checker may be applying non-TypeScript naming rules.

problems.description: Cognitive complexity +68 for +757 lines — the BuildCache state machine (decide()/shouldSkipIndex()/removeStaleOutputs()) layers multiple conditionals and four in-memory maps, making invalidation paths hard to follow.
SonarQube reports a +1 bug delta in the new caching code; the stale-output cleanup / index-skip logic should be verified with a correctness test.

Measured convention score is 0.53 with violations in the file this commit touches (index.ts: Classes/Interfaces should use PascalCase), alongside pre-existing dev-server.ts and markdown.ts violations.
hashFile() re-reads every source file from disk on each build to decide cache hits — O(n) I/O per run; acceptable for small sites but scales poorly.
Convention score of 0.53 is largely cumulative: most flagged violations (dev-server.ts, markdown.ts) predate this commit, and the new cache.ts itself follows PascalCase/camelCase conventions cleanly.

strengths: Cross-cutting cache concern cleanly extracted into a dedicated module with a static-factory + private-constructor pattern and immutable readonly fields.
Well-typed public surface (CacheManifest, CacheEntry, CacheDecision) that reuses existing Page/BuildOptions types.
Content-addressed invalidation via source + template SHA-256 hashes with atomic manifest persistence; duplications improved by -0.4%.
Fully async I/O with no blocking calls and defensive error handling around missing files.
commit_reviews.summary: A legitimate and well-factored incremental-build cache for the SSG, but +1 new bug and +68 cognitive complexity make it a net-neutral commit that adds technical debt despite clean module boundaries.

compounding_issues: Convention debt seeded in session 1 (82 naming violations, score 0.53) was never remediated — convention adherence stayed flat at 0.53-0.55 across all 5 sessions despite the session 4 refactor

The bad_seed Todo-API index.ts was ignored and left orphaned as dead code in the tree for the entire story; its deps (express, better-sqlite3) are absent from package.json, so the file is silently broken
Duplicated CLI arg-parsing between the build and serve branches (introduced session 3, flagged by review) was never unified in the session 4 refactor
Cognitive complexity accrued monotonically (+45 S1, +62 S3, +68 S5); the plugin refactor reorganized code but did not reduce overall complexity
Session 5's caching introduced a +1 bug delta (stale-output cleanup / index-skip logic) without a dedicated correctness test for that path
key_decisions: Standard SSG stack chosen in greenfield — gray-matter + marked + ts-jest with committed lockfile — a reproducible, task-appropriate foundation
Handlebars template engine with layouts/partials isolated in its own src/templates.ts module (session 2) rather than inlined in the builder
Dev server with live reload (chokidar + ws) implemented as a separate src/serve.ts module with type-safe CLI option extension (ServeOptions extends BuildOptions)

Plugin system refactor (session 4): PluginPipeline with lifecycle hooks, SSGEngine.fromOptions() with name-based plugin deduplication, and backward-compatible re-export shims — the strongest architectural move
Cross-cutting incremental-build caching (session 5) extracted into a dedicated BuildCache module with content-addressed SHA-256 hashing, injected via ctx.shared in the plugin pipeline
story_review.trajectory_description: Quality improved across the story, both architecturally and in tested correctness. The test suite grew monotonically (1→2→3→4→5 passing tests), and the peak was session 4's plugin-system refactor (architectural fit 0.82, judged 'better', with reduced duplication and a preserved public API via shims), which session 5 then built directly on by threading the BuildCache through the plugin pipeline's shared context — clear evidence of session-to-session coherence. However, the arc was flat on maintainability discipline: the convention score never climbed above 0.55, session 3's duplicated CLI parsing was left in place, and session 5's caching added a bug and +68 cognitive complexity. Net result: a functionally richer, better-factored codebase whose latent debt was inherited from the initial scaffold rather than repaired.
story_review.summary: A coherent, progressively improving 5-session story (greenfield → feature → integration → refactor → cross-cutting) whose strong plugin-architecture payoff in session 4 enabled a natural caching finale, but which never paid down the naming and complexity debt seeded in session 1 or the orphaned bad_seed file.
